name: Recursive Decision-Ledger Walk
description: Blueprint 24 of 96 (design card BP-REQ-02, 09-WORKFLOW-BLUEPRINT-LIBRARY.md:1225). MECHANISM: walk a DEPENDENT decision tree through an explicit FRONTIER, where answering a node EXPANDS its children per the dependency rules and every node write is a checkpoint - so a session loss resumes from the frontier, never from the root. A subtree that a parent answer makes moot is PRUNED WITH ITS REASON RECORDED, so reversing the parent restores it instead of silently losing it. Resume is not a convenience here; it is the load-bearing property, which is why the blueprint carries an explicit kill-and-resume drill and a restore gate rather than asserting resumability.

root_decision.description: The root question. Everything else is reached by expansion, not by enumeration.

dependency_rules.description: How an answer expands into children. Explicit, because an implicit expansion rule makes the tree unauditable.

ledger_path.description: The durable recursive ledger. Every node write lands here before the next node is asked.

max_depth.description: Depth bound. The design card contraindicates this blueprint when the tree is unknowably deep, so the bound is explicit rather than implied.

resume_drill.description: Run the kill-and-resume drill as part of the walk. Resumability is the load-bearing claim, so it is measured rather than asserted.

frontier-walker.description: Holds the frontier, asks the next node, and expands children strictly per the declared dependency rules

pruner.description: Prunes a subtree the parent answer made moot and RECORDS WHY, so a later reversal can restore it

checkpointer.description: Writes each node to the durable ledger and verifies the write before the walk advances

owner.description: The human owner - answers each frontier node; a wrong early answer invalidates a subtree, which is why prunes are recorded rather than applied destructively

stages.title: S0 SEED the root and initialise the frontier

work_unit.title: Seed the root decision node and write the initial frontier
work_unit.question_or_target: Write the root node and an explicit frontier containing exactly it, plus the parsed dependency rules and the depth bound.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: the frontier is the resume anchor; seeding it wrong makes every later resume wrong

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the seed records the root node id, the frontier as an explicit list, the depth bound and a hash of the dependency rules - so a rules change mid-walk is detectable rather than silently effective
tests_required: the initial frontier must contain exactly one node
a dependency-rules change mid-walk must be detected by the rules hash
both-states control: alter the rules hash and confirm the change is DETECTED; leave it and confirm it is not
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the checkpointer confirms the seed is on disk before the first node is asked
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:WREQ-0201 emitted when tree.json exists, parses, and carries a single-node frontier plus the rules hash; otherwise FAILED:WREQ-0201 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: no retry after the first node is answered - reseeding would discard answers; resume instead

stages.title: S1-S4 WALK the frontier: ask, expand, prune-with-reason, checkpoint, repeat until the frontier is empty

body.title: S1 ASK the next frontier node
body.prompt: This is the next node on the frontier. Answering it may expand children or prune a subtree; a prune is recorded with its reason and stays restorable if you later reverse this answer.

body.title: S2 EXPAND children per the dependency rules, and PRUNE what the answer made moot

work_unit.title: Expand children per the rules and record any prune with its reason
work_unit.question_or_target: Apply the dependency rules to the answer: add the children it unlocks to the frontier, and mark as PRUNED - never delete - any subtree the answer made moot, recording why.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: a silently dropped subtree is unrecoverable once the parent answer is reversed

work_unit.evidence_requirement: every added child cites the rule that produced it and every pruned node carries status PRUNED plus the answer that made it moot; a pruned node retains its full text so a reversal restores it
tests_required: a pruned node must retain status PRUNED and its text, never be deleted
reversing a parent answer must RESTORE the pruned subtree
a child added with no citing rule must be rejected - expansion may not be improvised
both-states control: delete a pruned node outright and confirm pruned-subtree-is-restorable FAILS; mark it PRUNED and confirm it PASSES
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the checkpointer verifies that node count never decreases across the walk
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:WREQ-0203 emitted per step when expansion.json exists, parses, every child cites a rule, and pruned_nodes_deleted == 0; otherwise FAILED:WREQ-0203 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: no retry that could double-expand; the idempotency key includes the node id

body.title: S3 CHECKPOINT - the node write must be durable before the walk advances

work_unit.title: Flush the node and the new frontier to the durable ledger and verify the write
work_unit.question_or_target: Write the answered node, the updated frontier and any prune records to the ledger, then READ THEM BACK and confirm they are durable before the walk advances.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: a write that was never flushed is indistinguishable from a write that never happened, and the whole resume claim rests on this

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the checkpoint records a read-back verification of the ledger after the write - existence plus a content hash - so durability is measured rather than assumed
tests_required: the walk must not advance until the read-back verification succeeds
nodes_written must equal nodes_checkpointed at every step
both-states control: simulate a failed flush and confirm every-node-write-is-a-checkpoint FAILS; a real flush must PASS
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: one independent reader confirms the checkpoint count equals the answered-node count at the end of the walk
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:WREQ-0204 emitted per step when the checkpoint artifact exists, parses, and the read-back hash matches the write; otherwise FAILED:WREQ-0204 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: one retry on a transient write failure; a second failure halts the walk rather than advancing on an unflushed node

stages.title: S3b Every node write was a checkpoint, or the resume claim is false
S3c Every prune carries a reason and nothing was deleted
S4 DRILL - kill the walk mid-flight and resume; the frontier must come back exactly

work_unit.title: Kill-and-resume drill - prove the frontier is restored exactly and not from the root
work_unit.question_or_target: Kill the walk after N answered nodes, resume it, and prove the restored frontier is byte-identical to the pre-kill frontier and that the walk did not restart from the root.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: the design card names this as the proof needed before adoption; resumability on this machine is UNVERIFIED without it

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the drill records the pre-kill frontier hash, the post-resume frontier hash, and the number of nodes re-asked - which must be zero; a drill that reports success without those three numbers proves nothing
tests_required: kill the session mid-walk and resume - the frontier must be exactly where it was
the resumed walk must re-ask ZERO already-answered nodes
both-states control: corrupt one checkpoint and confirm the drill FAILS; run it on intact checkpoints and confirm it PASSES - a drill that passes in both states measures nothing
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: one independent reader compares the two frontier hashes and confirms they match
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:WREQ-0205 emitted when resume-drill.json exists, parses, and pre-kill and post-resume frontier hashes match with zero nodes re-asked; otherwise FAILED:WREQ-0205 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: no retry - a failed resume drill is the finding, and re-running it with the same checkpoints is the same measurement

stages.title: S4b The resume must land on the frontier, not the root

impact.blast_radius: writes only under command-center/ledger-walk/bp-req-02/**; the ledger is append-and-mark, never delete, so a wrong early answer is recoverable

x_extensions.distinct_mechanism: an explicit frontier queue whose size IS the convergence metric, rule-cited expansion (improvised children rejected), prune-by-marking so a subtree stays restorable, a read-back-verified checkpoint per node, and a kill-and-resume drill with a both-states control that must fail on a corrupted checkpoint
x_extensions.not_a_duplicate_because: BP-REQ-01 asks a FLAT ordered list ranked foundational-first; this manages a DEPENDENT tree with a frontier and prunable subtrees, where answering a node CHANGES which nodes exist. It is the only blueprint in this range with no council and no fan-out at all, and the only one where resume is a gated, drilled property rather than a policy block.
contraindications: a flat list of independent choices - a plain grill is cheaper and this adds tree machinery for nothing
the tree is unknowably deep - the depth bound would fire immediately and the emit-partial is not useful

worked_examples.name: a dependent scoping tree where the root answer prunes a whole subtree

params.root_decision: Is a blueprint a schema-validated JSON definition, or a prose design card

prune: what prose template do cards use

expand_to: what prose template do cards use
do we accept the 328 currently-failing units
who fixes the non-canonical assignment shapes

worked_examples.walkthrough: S0 seeds one root node and hashes the three rules. Step 1 asks the root; the owner answers json-definition. S2 adds the four children the rule cites and marks the two prose-card nodes PRUNED with the reason `parent answered json-definition` - their text is retained. S3 writes and reads back the ledger; nodes_written == nodes_checkpointed == 1. Step 2 asks `which schema profile gates it`; the answer strict-profile expands two more children. The walk continues to depth 3, frontier_size falls to 0 at step 7 of a 400 bound. S3b confirms 7 written == 7 checkpointed. S3c confirms 2 prunes, both with reasons, 0 deletions. S4 kills the walk after node 4 and resumes: the pre-kill frontier hash matches the post-resume hash and zero nodes are re-asked. Then the owner reverses the root to prose-card - and because the two pruned nodes were MARKED rather than deleted, they are restored to the frontier while the json-definition subtree is pruned in turn.

expected_gate_outcomes.pruned-subtree-is-restorable: PASS - 2 prunes with reasons, 0 nodes deleted
expected_gate_outcomes.resume-lands-on-the-frontier: PASS - frontier hashes match, 0 nodes re-asked

worked_examples.name: negative control - a corrupted checkpoint must fail the drill

params.root_decision: Is a blueprint a schema-validated JSON definition, or a prose design card

worked_examples.walkthrough: One checkpoint file is truncated before the resume. The post-resume frontier hash no longer matches the pre-kill hash, resume_restored_frontier_exactly goes false, and resume-lands-on-the-frontier escalates to the owner rather than continuing on a frontier that silently lost a node. This is the both-states arm that makes the drill meaningful: a drill that reports PASS on a corrupted checkpoint would be measuring nothing, and the design card's stated proof-before-adoption would be satisfied by a probe that cannot fail.

benchmark_cases: kill the session mid-walk and resume - the frontier must be exactly where it was
reverse a parent answer - the pruned subtree must be restorable
x_extensions.unverified: UNVERIFIED resume behaviour on this machine; the settling experiment is the kill-and-resume drill, which this blueprint runs as a stage rather than leaving to trust. Corpus confidence band: very-likely (80-90%); estimate.confidence carries the nearest legal DSL band, likely.
x_extensions.confidence_band_note: The DSL confidence_band enum has five members and no very-likely, so the corpus band is recorded here and estimate.confidence carries likely (55-80%).
